t:
These notes were found on a pirate ship. A bunch of smaller notes written by the crew is attached. The text is only partially preserved:

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 23, 1018

Pirates captured me! This is so exciting!

Found several new tablets in Takalik Harbor. Since I'm imprisoned in this stinky cargo hold anyway, I have time to continue translating the tablets.

"Oh, glorious June Itsmal! Oh, great cities of Uskul and Miktlan! They have fallen to the fury of the June Curse. There's no escape. The curse cannot be lifted. There's nowhere to run. Almost all golems have been shattered. The portal network is destroyed.

We have only one way out left. The Dark One promised us salvation. He was the one to warn us about danger. If we'd killed treacherous Sheratan, the last Fire Dragon, the world could split in two, like a giant egg.

Wise Shilonen, Coatl, and Atslan want to seek assistance with him. There are those who oppose. Tka-a-Lithan Ric-ti-a-Nic, also known as Bane of the Fire Dragons, does not trust the Dark One. He suggests we return to the city and use the old portals."

The note stops abruptly. I hope I can steal the key when the goblin brings me food.

"Bosun's Notes"

"Bloody captain!
Well, we captured a ship of this elvish girl. It carried heaps of cargo! 21 silk cushions!
And the elvish girl was so pretty, leggy and all.
Just when the crew got excited, he tossed her overboard! And the cushions, too.
What a nasty piece of work!"

"We arrived at the Pirate Outpost. I say, that's where all the action is!

You can find all kinds of ships here. Some of them I haven't even seen out there, in the Astral. There were the Lord, and the Breath of Void, and the Striga! Breathtaking! We didn't have much time, though. We had some cargo to sell. Something that we brought from the Dead Sea.

We sealed the deal on July {num2}. This day will be remembered! We haven't made this much, like... ever!"

"Sailing Master's Notes"

"Bloody captain!

The June treasure will do us no good, no doubt!

I hear, Junes are cursed people. They brought demons to our world.

Captain shouldn't have gotten involved..."

"First Mate's Notes"

"Bloody captain!

We got ourselves into some dirty business. Here's how it happened. We made it to a port and got ashore. First thing we did was go down to the tavern. There was this fat bearded man in boots. Couldn't put down his newspaper.

So, he spotted our captain, beckoned him with a finger, and offered a good price for that crazy girl jumping about the ruins.

Captain was going to say no, but the money clouded his mind, his eyes lit up! He couldn't turn it down."

"Captain's Notes"

"Oh, these lovers of June artifacts!

Everybody wants this junk. They keep looking for something new.

We got this order from Simon on Suslanger. He wanted the June crystals, whatever they are. We had to sneak around for a week, hiding from trolls. They don't give a damn what they eat. One of them caught Mum Bad Ear, and the cracking bones was the last we heard. Finally, we delivered the crystals to the Great Mage.

Just as we were going to leave, Antoinette de Delice from Ignis sent a messenger, asking, and I quote, "My dear sailors, bring me some obsidian blades." Which means, we get to dig dirt to collect them. Here are you blades, your Mageness.

We kept some for ourselves, though. There's still plenty left in the ruins. Especially in hidden caches."

"Letter from the Great Mage Maximillian de Blizare"

"There's an unusual place somewhere in the Astral. The place where the Junes once fought two Great Dragons.

Having defeated most of the dragons, the Junes began to chase the remaining dragons around the world. Their sea vessels carrying mighty golems moved incredibly fast with magic. And the Dragon Hunters themselves were equally mighty.

And so the fleet ran down the two strongest dragons, the Great Dragons Tegmin and Rukbat. It was a great battle. The Junes suffered huge losses but managed to win.

Such creatures have so much magic accumulated in them that their death takes its toll. The last outburst of dragons' magic power froze a whole ocean! The cataclysm that happened later split the world in two, but the dragons' hearts kept the icy ocean intact. Magic turned the ocean into a burial vault for the two winged monsters, sending it floating into the Astral.

For centuries, this place was hidden from people's eyes until a pirate expedition came across the snow-covered dragon skeletons. The astral forces were eating away at the ice, exposing the secret lying underneath. Even beyond death the dragons' hearts are bleeding. The blood itself possesses some magical qualities. A Great Mage that drinks it will become immortal.

Although ordinary people have no idea, the icy allod immediately attracted the Treasure Hunters' attention.

The pirates will do anything to get into the icy tomb..."

"Quartermaster's Journal"

"[Written in irregular block letters.]

Rum. I need rum...

Got to get to the cargo hold. There's a whole barrel.

 Hic... Rum. Captain gives us no rum. He's been saving it.

All we are saying is give people rum!

…

 Gotta put down something else before I forget.

 I've seen a monster. A real monster, I swear.

 That isn't something you'd easily forget. Even rum doesn't help. It was right there, all they way up.

Gotta get some more rum... "

"Cook's Journal"

"Enough of it, I'm telling you!

Captain gets the profit. We'll lose our lives over nothing.

We shouldn't get involved with that. No searching for damned June artifacts in that dead city!
We must be careful, or else we could end up becoming eternal ghost-like wanderers of the astral seas, without being able to taste food or feel the breeze!

Let's start a riot! Throw captain over board along with the June trinkets!"

"Cabin Boy's Journal"

"I know captain's got a stash!

I saw him approach it. He pushed something, and the stash opened.

I've got to check it out when nobody's around.

If there's gold, I'll just sneak out quietly and go on the run.

Captain's been holding grudge after that girl wandered away under my supervision, he could throw me overboard."

t:
Let's get back to Marianna's notes:

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 18, 1018

I'm so angry! It took me a while to catch this idiot! Thank Tensess, I've got the tablets now. And this is the missing part!

I restored the missing fragment. It's a story of the great fall of the city June Itsmal.

"For the city was great and the citizens were proud. Gifts were brought to June Itsmal from all over the world. Beautiful ships arrived at Takalik harbor. The ruler of June Itsmal, the great Xolocipilli, was brave and wise. He used to hunt fire dragons.

Everything changed in one day. The Curse came to the city. The walls were tall, the gates were strong, but all defenses fell. The Curse took lives with just one stare. Mighty golems taller than the tallest trees have come to battle. But even they couldn't stop the Curse. The towers fell. Xolocipilli's palace fell and buried the city ruler underneath. Only a few survivors escaped the ruins of June Itsmal in the dead of night."

What happened next? Whoever wrote this, they clearly survived! I need to find the next piece...

I asked around if anything interesting was found lately. People tell me they heard a working girl brag about a pretty stone with strange inscriptions.  Not much of a lead, but that's all I have.

At least it's not boring..."

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 19, 1018

I think I'm onto something. An elf told me about a battle between goblins and the Free Traders' Mercenaries that took place recently. It sounds serious.

Louis also shared a couple of useful contacts. Someone's been tracking down June artifacts. And that someone was spotted asking the mercenaries about any interesting recent findings. Perhaps he was the one to hire goblins.

Well, anyway, those bastards wanted to break into Asee-Teph. It was quite a fight! Rocks falling everywhere, arrows flying around, swords clanging. I wish I could have seen it!

Unfortunately, this means that those tablets will be very hard to find.

t:
Here is a very interesting note from one of the pilgrims who got some of the tablets:

"My beloved Nancy!

I'm leaving you this note in case you start looking for me. Our holy father Ivan, the Devotee, advised me to visit the place known for its holiness. The first Chapel of Tensess! A great miracle happened here. Suddenly, an evil astral demon appeared and smashed the ship! But those who died in the Astral were brought back to life by the grace of Tensess. They appeared right here!

The chapel is nailed shut and abandoned. It upsets me greatly. I know that Goblins are to blame! They're wicked creatures, thieves and cheats! I heard an interesting story about them, though. They say that the ship that got wrecked in the Astral was carrying two goblins. They went into the Purgatory. One of them saw a Servant of Tensess and got scared! He started confessing his sins, promising to make an offering of Mirra. The other goblin heard that and offered to sell him Mirra! And it's been like this ever since: one goblin received Tensess's forgiveness and became a gift collector; the other goblin was cursed and banished from the Purgatory forever.

Well, one way or the other, my beloved Nancy, I should visit the smugglers. Give them a talking-to. Why have they neglected the Chapel? The mongers have the guts to collect money from pilgrims! Their leader lives somewhere around here. I should find him.

I will see you soon, my darling. I miss you. I'll return to you as soon as I sort this thing out."
